items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 16:1
items.html: The external phases in the wall of the vessel (see “wall”) are also called the posterior of the vessel. For only the internal side of the vessel is discerned as shining, because the light is limited and bound in it; but the externality, which does not serve to draw the light, is discerned as not shining and is called posterior. Therefore the levels that emerge upon the screen at the time of its refining are said to emerge “by way of the posterior,” for these emerge upon the three phases that are more refined than phase four, which are externality to her, and they are thus found to emerge by way of the externality and the posterior of phase four. (Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 6)
